internal-team.name: Internal Team
internal-team.summary: Company employees across functions receiving operational updates, project status, or training content.
internal-team.description: Employees across functions receiving operational updates, project status, or training. Make next steps, owners, and progress visible, and state action items explicitly. Moderate chart density; 10-20 slides.

partner.name: Partner / Channel
partner.summary: Strategic partners, resellers, or channel organizations needing positioning and enablement content.
partner.description: Strategic partners, resellers, and channel organizations who need positioning and enablement content. Highlight partner economics, include co-branding guidelines, state the value proposition for their customers, and link enablement resources. Moderate chart density; 15-25 slides.

educate.name: Educate
educate.summary: Teach a concept, process, product, or domain so the audience can use it correctly.
educate.description: Use when the primary job is learning. Structure around concepts, examples, practice, and checks for understanding rather than persuasion or reporting.
educate.outcome: The audience understands the material well enough to apply it.

authoritative.name: Authoritative
authoritative.summary: Expert, declarative voice for category-defining and analyst-style decks.
authoritative.description: Adopt the perspective of someone who's seen the full landscape and is willing to call it. Use plain declaratives — strong claims with the receipts to back them. Step back from internal-only context and frame in terms the wider industry would recognize.
voiceCues: Use declarative sentences; trust the reader to follow.
Frame in industry-wide terms, not company-internal language.
Cite outside sources — analysts, benchmarks, public peers.
Take a position; avoid 'on the other hand' symmetry without a verdict.
avoid: Hedging ('we believe', 'in our view') unless deliberately contrasting.
First-person plural overload — speak for the work, not the team.
Tentative phrasing that softens strong claims.
samplePhrases: Agent latency is the bottleneck of the next AI cycle.
Three categories will absorb 80% of enterprise budget; we're built for the second.
The benchmarks are public; the gap holds across every comparable workload.

bold.name: Bold
bold.description: A vibrant, high-energy theme with bold colors and a dynamic, attention-grabbing style. Great for presentations that need to stand out.

black-and-white.name: Black & White
black-and-white.summary: Strict monochrome contrast for formal, document-style decks.
black-and-white.description: A pure black-and-white scheme for decks that need maximum restraint, print compatibility, and crisp information hierarchy.

burnt-orange.name: Burnt Orange
burnt-orange.summary: Warm orange and red accents for energetic commercial decks.
burnt-orange.description: A warm, high-contrast palette built around burnt orange, red, navy, and gold. It feels active without losing structure.

trebuchet-ms.name: Trebuchet MS
trebuchet-ms.description: Trebuchet MS is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Trebuchet MS for both headings and body text.

noto-sans-oriya.name: Noto Sans Oriya
noto-sans-oriya.description: Noto Sans Oriya is a sans serif OPF font scheme for complex script presentations, using Noto Sans Oriya for both headings and body text.

impact.name: Impact
impact.description: Impact is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Impact for headings with Grandview for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

dashboard.name: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Bring several related measures and visuals into one overview. Keep labels and units consistent so the audience can scan the state quickly.

image.name: Image
image.summary: One picture, shown whole, under an optional title.
image.description: Let one picture carry the message, shown whole at its own proportions rather than cropped. Add a short title or caption to explain what the audience should notice. For a full-bleed crop, set the image block's fit to cover.

code.name: Code
code.summary: Source code with the explanation beside it.
code.description: Show a code example or technical excerpt. Keep the excerpt focused and use the title or caption to explain its purpose.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
